2607.25032.title: Authoring Agent Skills: A Software-Engineering Approach
2607.25032.paper_summary: Agent Skills are an emerging way to extend large language model agents with reusable procedural knowledge that the agent loads on demand. Anthropic introduced Agent Skills and published the format as an open specification supported across several agent tools. This note argues that a skill is a software artefact and that its construction should follow software-engineering principles, with qualifications: single responsibility, separation of interface from implementation, low coupling, and economy in a shared token budget, together with behavioural evaluation in place of deterministic testing. Using Claude Code as the reference implementation, it describes how a skill is structured, how its contents are loaded in stages, and how to write the description on which selection depends. It places skills against the other mechanisms a developer can use to shape agent behaviour, like project memory files, slash commands, subagents, external tool connections, and hooks, and gives a rule for choosing between them based on who decides that a mechanism runs and what guarantee it provides. It then sets out an evaluation-driven authoring process, a set of patterns and faults commonly encountered in authoring, and the trust question raised by using skills from third parties. We illustrate the comparison drawn in UML class style, the loading model, the anatomy of a skill, the relative position of each mechanism, and the points at which skills and hooks act during a session.
2607.25032.paper_summary_zh: 代理技能是一種新興方式，旨在擴展大型語言模型代理，並提供可重用的程序知識，該知識由代理按需加載。Anthropic 引入了代理技能，並將該格式發布為一個開放規範，支持多個代理工具。這份說明認為，技能是一種軟體工件，其構建應遵循軟體工程原則，具備以下條件：單一責任、接口與實現的分離、低耦合，以及在共享令牌預算中的經濟性，並用行為評估取代確定性測試。以 Claude Code 作為參考實現，描述了技能的結構、內容如何分階段加載，以及如何撰寫選擇所依賴的描述。它將技能與開發者可以用來塑造代理行為的其他機制進行比較，例如項目記憶文件、斜線命令、子代理、外部工具連接和鉤子，並根據誰決定機制運行及其提供的保證給出選擇之間的規則。接著，它提出了一個以評估為驅動的創作過程、一組在創作中常見的模式和故障，以及使用第三方技能所引發的信任問題。我們以 UML 類樣式展示比較，載入模型、技能的解剖、每個機制的相對位置，以及技能和鉤子在會話期間作用的點。
2607.25032.author: Giuseppe Destefanis et.al.
